transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-01
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samira Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Markus Jensen (CedarBridge - Procurement), Anika Shah (CedarBridge - Legal), Diego Rivera (CedarBridge - Platform), Lina Park (CedarBridge - Finance)
Recording: Zoom

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Purpose: align legal/procurement on pilot contracting path (MSA/DPA), SLA targets, pricing approval lane and technical preflight for a 2-week pilot.
- Key concerns: data residency / PHI handling, KMS/egress costs, rollback SLA, indemnity language in MSA.
- Outcome: Redwood to deliver redlines, pilot runbook, connectivity checklist; CedarBridge to return DPA exceptions and confirm procurement cadence.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes — um — to cover contracting runway and the pilot preflight. We're Alex from Redwood, Priya SE and Samira on the CSM side. Markus, Anika, Diego, Lina from CedarBridge, thanks for making the time.
[00:22] Markus Jensen: Yeah thanks Alex. Quick ask — procurement wants a clear gating list, timeline and egress cost examples, so we can present to finance.
[00:34] Alex Chen: Totally, we'll put those in the packet. Priya, do you want to run through pilot scope so legal knows what to expect?
[00:41] Priya Nair: Sure, super quick. Pilot is a two week technical evaluation, low volume, we recommend Hosted API to start then optional Dedicated if you need predictable throughput. We will provide an infra runbook: endpoints, token lifecycle, KMS options. For CedarBridge specifically, we noted PHI-ish workloads so private deployment was discussed — and we'll show a VPC peering checklist.
[01:12] Anika Shah: When you say private deployment, is that private control-plane or full on-prem? Our security team asked about HSM support and whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS.
[01:24] Priya Nair: Yes we support customer KMS integrations (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer bring-your-key via managed KMS in our region — but if you need on-prem we can run a private bundle. I'll attach the options matrix.
[01:45] Diego Rivera: Clarify please — latency SLAs if we go Hosted vs Dedicated? Our SLA requirements for the pilot are 99.9 for uptime and percentile latency for the short seq is important.
[02:00] Alex Chen: Right. For Hosted we offer best-effort latency targets in the pilot, not SLA-backed. Dedicated comes with SLA targets and a capacity reservation. We can provide historical percentiles for comparable workloads — we'll include a latency profile doc.
[02:18] Lina Park: And pricing. Finance needs egress examples, token cost, plus what happens if we go Dedicated mid-pilot — is there a pro-rata?
[02:30] Alex Chen: There's a pro-rata model for capacity commits; we'll show two scenarios — continued Hosted, or transition to Dedicated with monthly commit. We'll include per-token examples and an estimated egress fee for multi-region replicates.
[02:47] Markus Jensen: From procurement perspective, the MSA has a standard indemnity clause that's causing pause. We need to know if Redwood will do liability caps tied to fees or separate carve-outs for data breaches.
[03:02] Samira Ortiz: We've seen that. Redwood's standard MSA has caps tied to fees and an explicit carve-out for gross negligence. Alex, want to state the standard position?
[03:13] Alex Chen: Yeah, Redwood's standard is a liability cap equal to 12 months of fees, with exceptions for willful misconduct and certain regulatory fines. We can discuss specific carve-outs but legal will need to review redlines.
[03:29] Anika Shah: Ok please send the standard MSA and DPA with a short summary of variable clauses — helps speed review. Also curious about audit logs and retention windows.
[03:40] Priya Nair: Audit logs are available, retention levels vary by plan; we'll include what fields are emitted and how long they're stored. For pilot we'd enable extended logging and give you x-day retention for debugging.
[03:56] Diego Rivera: Connectivity — do you support cross-account VPC peering or Transit Gateway? We prefer to avoid public egress for PHI token exchange.
[04:08] Priya Nair: We support VPC peering and private endpoints; Transit GW is supported via config. The checklist will have steps: CIDR ranges, NAT, routing, firewall rules, and a small sample Terraform snippet.
[04:28] Markus Jensen: Procurement asks for a clear 'go/no-go' decision gate 14 days after contract sign — if legal isn't done by then we still need to have fallback options.
[04:39] Alex Chen: That's reasonable; we can include a conditional clause in the SOW that prescribes a 14-day legal review window and an extension path. For fallback, we can run a sandbox hosted instance with restricted dataset until private prep is done.
[04:57] Anika Shah: DPA exceptions — we typically ask for a list of non-negotiable terms, e.g., data residency and deletion SLA. Will Redwood accept an explicit deletion window for PHI?
[05:10] Priya Nair: We can accept deletion SLA clauses; we'll propose 30/90 day windows depending on deployment type. For Hosted, 30 days is typical; for Private/on-prem we can do immediate deletion on request. We'll document the exact API calls for data erasure.
[05:28] Alex Chen: I'll note that in the MSA/DPA packet.
[05:35] [07:00] Samira Ortiz: (interruption/background) there's a couple of procurement items — Markus, wanted to confirm who the signatory will be?
[07:10] Markus Jensen: Likely me for procurement sign-off, general counsel will do final legal sign off.
[07:17] Lina Park: Finance want a cap on egress spend for pilot — can Redwood provide a billing cap alerting mechanism?
[07:26] Alex Chen: Yes we have quota and alerting; we can set a hard cap for pilot and notify stakeholders. We'll show a sample billing alert configuration in the packet.
[07:40] Diego Rivera: On the technical eval — can Redwood run a short benchmark with our sample dataset? We want to measure latency and per-token cost for sequence lengths ~512.
[07:52] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Two options: we run a controlled benchmark on Hosted with synthetic tokens, or we give you a benchmark harness to run in your environment. If PHI is involved, we'd prefer you run the harness in your environment or we use an anonymized extract.
[08:12] Anika Shah: If we run it on Redwood's side, we'll need a data processing agreement addendum.
[08:18] Alex Chen: Understood — we'll add a limited DPA addendum for benchmarking.
[08:24] [12:00] Markus Jensen: A procurement-specific question: do you support net-60 payments or is net-30 standard? And what about escrow for code or models?
[12:12] Alex Chen: Standard is net-30. For enterprise, net-45/60 is negotiable based on contract size; escrow for models is not typical since we serve models as a managed inference runtime, but we can discuss escrow or code escrow for on-prem bundles.
[12:30] Lina Park: Good to know.
[12:35] Diego Rivera: Regarding RBAC and SSO — SAML/Okta? We need RBAC that maps to groups and audit events for security reviews.
[12:44] Priya Nair: We support SAML SSO (Okta, Azure AD), role-based permissions, and token-scoped keys. Audit events include request metadata and model selection. We'll send the schema for audit logs.
[12:58] Anika Shah: Can you also confirm SOC 2 attestation timeline? We require SOC 2 Type II or equivalent controls report for production use.
[13:08] Alex Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II — current report updated 2025-Q1. We'll attach the cert and an overview of controls.
[13:18] Markus Jensen: Are there any red flags from Redwood's side on our SLAs? We typically require a rollback policy if model quality drops.
[13:28] Priya Nair: We can include a rollback and canary rollout clause in the SOW; Optimize monitors for quality regressions tied to eval sets. We can define regression thresholds and automatic rollback to previous pinned model.
[13:44] Alex Chen: Also for the pilot we suggest a quality monitor on a small prompt set with scheduled evaluations, we'll share a template.
[13:55] Diego Rivera: One more technical — does Redwood allow KV cache persistence across warm restarts? We want to avoid cold-start penalties for our user flows.
[14:05] Priya Nair: The runtime supports KV cache persistence strategies on Dedicated; for Hosted we have warmed caches heuristics but persistence is limited. We'll document cache behavior per deployment type.
[14:22] Samira Ortiz: Quick note — legal likes to see a simple SLO table up front with error budget and remedies. Alex, can we make that a one pager?
[14:30] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll add a one-page SLO table with 99.9 uptime for Dedicated, sample latency percentiles, and the remediation tiers (credits / root cause / escalations).
[14:44] [20:00] Anika Shah: About indemnity — our counsel wants a carve-out for data breaches tied to vendor negligence. Is Redwood open to narrowing the carve-outs?
[20:12] Alex Chen: We'll take that back; Redwood's legal can consider narrowing certain carve-outs. We can't remove all caps but can negotiate exceptions.
[20:24] Markus Jensen: Procurement also wants a clause for termination for convenience during pilot with no termination fee. Is that typical?
[20:33] Alex Chen: For pilots we usually allow termination for convenience with a short notice period and no long-term penalties — we'll formalize that.
[20:44] Diego Rivera: For the pilot SOW, what telemetry are you asking us to provide for the eval? We'll prefer minimal sample data and synthetic loads.
[20:55] Priya Nair: Minimal: sample prompt set, sequence-length distribution, expected concurrency; we'll provide a small JSON template for that.
[21:07] Lina Park: Can Redwood provide an estimate of monthly cost at 1M tokens/month and potential savings if we enable batching/quantization?
[21:17] Alex Chen: We'll supply two cost models: baseline per-token with standard model and an optimized path using batching + quantization with estimated percent savings.
[21:27] Samira Ortiz: (note) Action owners and deadlines — we'll capture in the follow-up email.
[21:34] [30:00] Alex Chen: Recap — Redwood to send: redlined MSA/DPA (standard + summary), pilot SOW draft, connectivity and VPC checklist, benchmark harness + sample runs, one-page SLO table, pricing scenarios. CedarBridge to return DPA exceptions and confirm signatory and procurement cadence.
[30:50] Markus Jensen: Sounds good. If we need a legal deep-dive we'll schedule a separate session with counsel.
[30:58] Anika Shah: Yep, we'll probably have a 45 minute legal-only session focused on indemnity and data residency.
[31:10] Alex Chen: Great. Any final clarifying questions?
[31:18] Diego Rivera: One last ask — can we get a sample connectivity test window in the runbook, like a dry-run checklist with estimated time (2–3 hours)?
[31:28] Priya Nair: Yep we'll include a 2–3 hour dry-run window with test cases.
[31:35] Lina Park: And please include billing contact and invoicing lead time so finance can prepare.
[31:41] Alex Chen: We'll include billing contacts and net-30/defaults and note negotiation levers.
[31:48] [43:00] Samira Ortiz: Thanks all — we'll wrap and follow up by email with attachments.
[43:08] Markus Jensen: Thanks everyone, talk to you soon.

End of recording.
